title: Vayeshev: the empty pit (Genesis 37:24)
hook: "the pit was empty, there was no water in it"

segments.voice: Yesterday, a man with no name who pointed Joseph to Dothan. Your line was someone points the way. This week: three ways to prepare, a limp, back to Bethel, Esau's family, wanting to settle, and the man in the field. Today, what waited at Dothan.

Some moments in life are just a hole. A diagnosis. A layoff. The night the house goes quiet after a divorce. You're at the bottom of something, and you can't see a way up. Joseph walks toward his brothers across the fields at Dothan, wearing the coat his father gave him. They see him coming from far off. Before he reaches them, they've already made a plan.
screen: `AT THE BOTTOM OF SOMETHING.` → `THE COAT, SEEN FROM FAR OFF.` → `A PLAN BEFORE HE ARRIVES.`

segments.voice: Here comes the dreamer, they say. Let's kill him, throw him into one of the pits, and say a wild animal ate him. Then we'll see what becomes of his dreams. Reuben, the oldest, steps in. Don't take his life. Throw him into this pit, here in the wilderness, but don't lay a hand on him. The Torah tells us why: Reuben meant to come back later and rescue him. So Joseph arrives, and they strip off his coat, the coat, and throw him into the pit. Then one flat detail, in the old Jewish Publication Society translation: "and the pit was empty, there was no water in it." Why tell us that? If it's empty, of course there's no water. The rabbis read the doubled phrase slowly. The Talmud says: there was no water in it, but there were snakes and scorpions. Empty of what helps, and not empty of what harms. Others hear it more plainly. It was a cistern for catching rain, and it was dry, so Joseph wouldn't drown. Empty can be terrible. It can also be the thing that keeps you alive. Then the next verse, flat and cold: the brothers sat down to eat bread. Their brother is in a hole nearby, and they have lunch. The story doesn't let us look away from that. Joseph is in the pit, stripped, alone, nothing in it but darkness. And, the story will show, it isn't the end of him.
screen: `HERE COMES THE DREAMER.` · `REUBEN: DON'T KILL HIM.` · `NO WATER, BUT SNAKES AND SCORPIONS.` · `THEY SAT DOWN TO EAT.` · then, large: `THE PIT WAS EMPTY.`

segments.voice: Where is there a dry pit in your life right now: a friendship that went quiet, a hope that ran out, a hole where a person used to be? Don't rush to fill it; just look at it honestly. Is it only empty, or is there something in there too, fear, or strength you didn't know you had?
Vayeshev. And he settled: the portion where Joseph's brothers throw him into a pit with no water in it, and then sit down to eat.
Your line: no water in it. One flat line, read slowly. That's day two hundred three.

howItsDone: The sale of Joseph is read in synagogues each winter in Vayeshev, and later Jewish tradition links the brothers' sin to the martyrdom of ten sages remembered on Yom Kippur.

fork.reveal: Reuben said, don't take his life, throw him into this pit. he planned to come back and rescue him.

original.note: Hebrew: a pit, a cistern for rainwater. Joseph's was dry.

what it means: Joseph at the lowest point, stripped and alone, while his brothers eat nearby.
what a scholar hears: the Talmud (Shabbat 22a) reads the doubled phrase: no water in it, but snakes and scorpions there were.
